A.name: The Missed-Call Leak
A.desc: Booking-process leak angle. Emergency wildlife caller is already panicking — your site loses them at the booking button before the phone even rings. $8K-$24K/mo anchor. Tease third issue. Dual-path close.

beats.title: I Hit a Wall on Your Site
beats.line: Hey — I was on your site a minute ago trying to get someone out for a raccoon in the attic, and I couldn't get through. Couldn't find a number to tap, the booking thing wouldn't go. Who handles the website over there? … Honestly, I'm glad you asked — because if it stopped me, it's stopping the homeowners you're paying to send there. That's about $8K to $24K a month in jobs walking to the next guy.
beats.followup: Got it — give me 30 seconds and I'll show you exactly where the leak is.
beats.note: COLD open, gatekeeper-disarm. You sound like a panicked customer, not a pitch — that's what gets you past the front desk to the owner. Say 'raccoon in the attic' with a little stress in your voice. The pivot ('glad you asked') is where you flip from prospect to auditor — land it warm, not gotcha. Then go straight into the 3-second window.

beats.title: Emergency Caller, 3-Second Window
beats.line: Here's the deal — when a homeowner hears something in the attic at night, they Google, tap the first ad, and decide in about 3 seconds whether they're calling you or moving on. Wildlife removal is emergency-service buying — that caller will hire the first shop that makes it easy to reach them. When was the last time someone on your team pulled up your site on a phone and tried to call or book right from it?
beats.followup: Yeah — that's the most common answer. The booking button is just the first leak. The bigger ones come after.
beats.note: Plain English. Emergency-service mindset. Ends with a question they can't confidently answer.

beats.title: The Booking Button Costs You the Job
beats.line: Here's what's actually happening. The homeowner taps your ad, counts to three, and your phone number isn't front and center — so they back out and tap the next shop. The next shop picks up, gets the job — and gets paid for it. The ones who do find your number land on a booking process that asks them to fill out a form before they've even said what's in their attic. By the time they figure it out, they've already called two other shops. That's the $8K to $24K a month. Getting your phone number visible and making it easy to book — those are week-one quick wins. But there's a third issue on your site that costs more than both of those combined. I'd rather show you that one with your page open.
responses: How much would this cost to fix?
beats.followup: Fair — and that's exactly what the audit answers. Pricing comes after.
beats.note: Tease the third issue. Do NOT reveal it on the call. The reveal is the audit. Dollar-anchor the competitor steal.

beats.title: 100+ Wildlife Sites, Same 3 Leaks
beats.line: I've done this on over 100 wildlife removal sites — same 10-point checklist, same booking process, same three leaks every time. The shops that fix the top two see calls climb in the first week. The ones that fix all three usually double their booked jobs inside 30 days.
responses: How long does the fix take?
beats.followup: Fair — and that's exactly why I lead with the audit, not the pitch.
beats.note: Credibility frame. 100+ sites. Same checklist. Pattern recognition.

beats.title: Free $1,500 Audit
beats.line: Here's what I want to do. I run a $1,500 conversion audit — and I'd like to do yours free. Thirty minutes. Your live site on screen. Every leak named in plain English no agency would dare use, with dollar-anchored estimates per leak — just the numbers, in your numbers. You walk away with a sequenced fix-list ranked by conversion impact and effort to ship — quick wins first. Yours to keep whether you hire me to ship it or not. Not vibes — math.
beats.followup: No catch — I'm running a handful of these personally this quarter for case studies. That's the only ask.
beats.note: Verbatim critterclick.com language throughout. $1,500 free. One-week plan. All fixes shipped at once.

beats.title: Calendar or Sample
beats.line: Here's how this works. I've got Thursday at 10 or Friday at 2 open — pick one and I'll send the calendar invite. Or, if you'd rather see what this looks like first, give me your email and I'll send over a sample audit I did for another wildlife removal shop — full fix-list, dollar numbers, the whole thing. Which one works for you?
beats.followup: Done — calendar invite or sample audit hits your inbox in 60 seconds.
beats.note: Dual-path close. Booked call OR sample audit. Either is a win.

D.name: Voicemails — EURO / PAS / NEPQ
D.desc: Three ready-to-leave voicemails, one per framework: EURO (Empathy·Urgency·Reason·Offer), PAS (Problem·Agitate·Solve), and NEPQ (a curiosity question that leaves an open loop). Each is ~20-25s and drives ONE low-friction CTA: text back and I’ll send a 60-second sample of your own page. Pick one per prospect; pair with the text follow-up shown under each.

beats.title: EURO — Empathy · Urgency · Reason · Offer
beats.line: Hey, it’s {caller} with CritterClick. Thirty seconds, I promise. I build phone-first pages for wildlife removal shops, and I pulled up yours — it’s quietly costing you around $8K to $24K a month in jobs you never see. Here’s the good part: it’s a fast fix, and I already rebuilt a 60-second sample of your own page so you can just look at it. Text me back at this number — no pitch, just the sample.
beats.followup: Text follow-up (send right after): “{caller} from CritterClick — here’s that 60-sec sample of your page I left you a VM about: [link]. Take a look when you get a sec.”
beats.note: EURO = Empathy (30 sec, I promise) → Urgency (fast fix) → Reason (jobs you never see) → Offer (the sample). Punchy and warm — smile while you talk, keep the energy up. Short breath-lines. Say the number slowly, twice. End on the offer.

beats.title: PAS — Problem · Agitate · Solve
beats.line: {caller} again with CritterClick. Picture it: 11pm, someone’s got something scratching in the attic, they find your site, they’re ready to book right now. But the page makes them dig for your number — so they bail and call the next guy. That’s not a traffic problem. That’s $8K to $24K a month walking out the door. Easiest fix there is — I’ve got a phone-first page where one tap calls you ready to show you. Text me back and I’ll send the sample.
beats.followup: Text follow-up: “{caller}, CritterClick — the fix for that 11pm caller problem, built on your own page: [link]. Worth a 60-sec look.”
beats.note: PAS = paint the Problem (the panicked 11pm caller) → Agitate (they call the next guy) → Solve (one-tap page). Lead with the vivid scene, not the dollar figure. Half-beat pause before the dollar number. Keep it upbeat, never doom.

beats.title: NEPQ — Curiosity Question
beats.line: Hey, {caller} with CritterClick — one honest question, then I’m gone. If your site was quietly costing you $8K to $24K a month in booked jobs, would you even know? Most owners don’t — the calls just don’t come, and you chalk it up to a slow month. I rebuilt a 60-second sample of your own page, and honestly, the gap surprised me. Text this number back and I’ll send it — worst case, you find out your page is already dialed in.
beats.followup: Text follow-up: “That question I left you — here’s the answer: [link]. 60-sec look at your page, rebuilt. Let me know what you think.”
beats.note: NEPQ = the status-quo question (would you even know?) opens a loop the callback closes. Do NOT answer it on the VM. Tone: genuinely curious, never gotcha. The self-effacing close (maybe it’s already dialed in) disarms resistance.
